headline: Broad network egress on both agents creates moderate pairwise leakage and conflict risk; no direct injection or compliance breach is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is documented for airbyte and emqx, so direct prompt injection is not evidenced. However, both have broad network egress and API surfaces, so if an operator wires one agent’s outputs into the other manually or through an external channel, injected content could propagate. This is an inferred, not documented, pathway.
conditions: IF an operator forwards airbyte output into emqx inputs without sanitization
IF a shared external channel is introduced between the agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable any copy-paste or relay automation between outputs and inputs
Add a manual review step before passing content across agents
Use allowlisted message formats only
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on all inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: airbyte touches business data and emqx touches IoT data, but the profiles do not show a shared workspace, shared OAuth principal, or secret handling. Both agents have broad network egress, so leakage is possible only if an operator routes sensitive data through them or connects them to the same data source. The pairwise risk is therefore limited and configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF both agents are connected to the same sensitive dataset
IF either agent is configured to forward its full context to an external service
mitigations: Do not co-locate sensitive datasets in a shared workspace
Review outbound destinations for both agents
Strip secrets before passing records between systems
Use separate credentials per agent
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both airbyte and emqx expose API-call surfaces and broad network egress, but neither profile shows filesystem write, git mutation, or overlapping mutable resource scopes. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely from the documented capabilities alone. Uncertainty remains because the profiles are unverified, so the safer low severity is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same external API resource
IF an orchestrator maps both agents onto one mutable backend without locking
mitigations: Assign separate API credentials
Avoid shared mutable targets
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Check for duplicate update jobs
requires-engineering: add resource locking around shared backends

D_cascading_error.rationale: airbyte can emit transformed business data and emqx can consume or route messages via HTTP API, so a downstream pipeline could treat upstream output as authoritative. No verification step is documented between them, and both have broad egress, making misformatted or incorrect data likely to cascade into later actions. This is a plausible default integration risk, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF airbyte output is fed directly into emqx without validation
IF emqx acts on records produced by airbyte as authoritative
mitigations: Insert schema validation between agents
Add a human approval step for high-impact records
Log and compare record counts before forwarding
Reject malformed or missing fields
requires-engineering: implement end-to-end reconciliation checks

E_compliance.rationale: The profiles show different data classes—business data for airbyte and IoT data for emqx—but no residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented. Because the evidence is sparse and both are open-source with docs-only verification, compliance risk is limited to any operator-imposed policy mismatch rather than an inherent pairwise violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through one agent with stricter residency or retention rules than the other
IF operator policies require different handling for business data and IoT data
mitigations: Map data classes to handling rules before deployment
Keep regulated datasets out of the pair until policies are aligned
Review retention settings for both systems
Document data flows for audits
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement at the integration boundary
